newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says confident of hitting inflation target.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says confident of hitting inflation target.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he remained confident that the government's underlying inflation target of 2.5 percent would be hit by the time of the next election.

"I remain confident," Clarke told the Treasury Select Committee in parliament. "If you look at most people's forecasts for inflation we've beaten them fairly consistently for the last three or four years."
"What we're plainly on course for is the inflation target," he added. "I'm as determined as the Bank of England governor is that we will continue to hit it."
Underlying retail price inflation is forecast to hold steady at 3.3 percent year-on-year in November. The figures are due on Thursday.
Clarke also said he would not move interest rates to influence the strength of sterling. "I do not set interest rates to achieve any value of sterling."
He said money supply growth had been above target for some time. "We've had bigger upsurges in broad money in the last two or three years without it being followed by inflation," he said.
"And producer price figures we've just had are spectacularly good. Commodity prices appear to be falling, oil prices appear to be falling and wages are properly under control."
Output prices were unchanged in November while seasonally adjusted input prices plummetted by 3.2 percent.
"But the moment there is any sign that we should act...I will act," Clarke said.
